result: A large, adequately diagnosed CFS sample showed clear cognitive impairment on an extensive battery, independent of psychopathology (no effect sizes given).
reason: Same construct and direction as the meta-analysis; abstract gives no numbers or domains, so low weight.

result: In primary care attenders, CDC-1994 CFS prevalence was 2.1% in London (n=2459) vs 1.6% in Sao Paulo (n=3914), P=0.20, but 11 cases had a recorded diagnosis in Britain and none in Brazil.
reason: Prevalence by criteria in a new cross-cultural setting, adding the gap between criteria-based prevalence and physician recognition; primary-care rate higher than population range.

result: Plasma CoQ10 was lower in 58 ME/CFS patients than 22 controls (p=0.00001), 44.8% fell below the lowest control value (490 ug/L), and levels correlated inversely with FibroFatigue total, fatigue and autonomic scores.
reason: Low CoQ10 in ME/CFS is covered by the newer omics-low-coq10 finding; check whether Maes 2009 is already cited there.

result: In a population-based case-control study (113 CFS, 124 controls), childhood trauma carried a 6-fold CFS risk, and decreased salivary cortisol after awakening appeared only in CFS patients with trauma exposure, not in those without.
reason: Same measure (awakening salivary cortisol); adds a subgroup showing that low cortisol tracks childhood trauma rather than CFS as a whole.

result: Over 2 years in a high-functioning cohort (n=75), fewer than 20% scored in the healthy adult range for fatigue impact and physical function; self-rated global improvement tracked momentary fatigue and standing frequency but not actigraphy.
reason: Healthy-range outcome at follow-up is a recovery-type measure and points the same way (recovery uncommon), though the study's focus is outcome measurement.

result: In 13 monozygotic female twin pairs discordant for CFS, sleep EEG spectral power did not differ in any band, and alpha-delta activity occurred in 5 CFS twins but also in 4 of their 5 healthy co-twins, despite more sleep complaints in the CFS twins.
reason: Tests the sleep microstructure (alpha intrusion) that the finding's detail calls promising and finds no disease effect; does not report the latency, WASO or efficiency in the claim.

result: Quantitative sleep EEG spectral power (delta through beta) showed no differences between CFS twins and healthy co-twins (13 pairs).
reason: Same qEEG spectral power measure with a null result, in a strong co-twin design; sleep rather than waking EEG.

result: In 41 CDC-defined CFS patients, diurnal salivary cortisol output (0800-2000 h) rose significantly after 15 sessions of CBT, together with clinical response; there was no untreated control group.
reason: Same measure; adds a time course consistent with the finding's caveat that low cortisol may be secondary, but uncontrolled.

result: On a 2-minute active stand, 27% (16/59) of Fukuda CFS/ME patients had POTS vs 9% of 52 matched controls (P=0.006); maximum standing HR was 106 vs 98 bpm (P=0.02).
reason: Independent cohort giving a POTS prevalence within the finding's 6-43% range.

result: POTS was found in 27% of 59 CFS/ME patients vs 9% of controls on a 2-minute active stand.
reason: Supports only the 'roughly a fifth have POTS' part; no cerebral perfusion or preload measured, and neuro-pots-prevalence is the better home.
